title: Streptococcus pneumoniae Endophthalmitis: Clinical Masterclass
summary: Streptococcus pneumoniae endophthalmitis is a hyper-acute, fulminant intraocular infection characterized by severe pain, rapid vision loss, and massive intraocular inflammation. Due to potent virulence factors like pneumolysin, immediate diagnostic tap, intravitreal antibiotic administration, and early surgical intervention are vital to preserve globe integrity and visual function.

sections.title: Definition & Clinical Overview
content: Acute, fulminant intraocular inflammation caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae (Gram-positive alpha-hemolytic lanceolate diplococci).
Presents with rapid-onset ocular pain, severe ciliary flush, dense hypopyon, and marked loss of visual acuity within 24 to 72 hours.
Clinical settings include post-cataract surgery, intravitreal anti-VEGF injections, post-trabeculectomy filtering bleb infections, and penetrating ocular trauma.

references.citation: Durand ML. Bacterial Endophthalmitis. N Engl J Med. 2017;377(14):1403-1404.
Miller JJ, et al. Endophthalmitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Ophthalmology. 2004;111(8):1555-1559.
Wykoff CC, et al. Endophthalmitis caused by Streptococcus species. Ophthalmology. 2011;118(6):1140-1146.

branches: Polysaccharide Capsule: Prevents opsonophagocytosis by neutrophils and macrophages
Pneumolysin (PLY): Cytolytic pore-forming toxin inducing retinal ganglion cell lysis
Autolysin (LytA): Triggers bacterial self-lysis, releasing inflammatory cell wall products
IgA1 Protease & H2O2: Facilitates mucosal surface adherence and oxidative ocular damage

references.citation: Ng EW, et al. Pneumolysin as a virulence factor in Streptococcus pneumoniae endophthalmitis. Curr Eye Res. 2002;24(4):282-288.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & Host Immune Response
sections.content: Intraocular introduction of S. pneumoniae rapidly triggers massive recruitment of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) into the vitreous cavity. Bacterial cell wall components (teichoic acid and peptidoglycan) activate Toll-like receptors (TLR2/TLR4), triggering a storm of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, IL-6). The combination of direct toxin toxicity (pneumolysin) and bystander damage from PMN degranulation induces rapid photoreceptor death and permanent visual impairment within 24–48 hours.

references.citation: Callegan MC, et al. Bacterial endophthalmitis: therapeutic challenges and host responses. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2007;26(2):189-203.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation & Symptoms
content: Rapid Onset: Symptoms typically begin 24-72 hours post-procedure or post-trauma.
Ocular Pain: Severe, deep throbbing periocular pain and pronounced photophobia.
Visual Loss: Rapid, profound drop in visual acuity to Light Perception (LP) or Hand Motion (HM).
External Signs: Eyelid edema, conjunctival hyperemia, and marked chemosis.

references.citation: Relhan N, et al. Endophthalmitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae: clinical features and outcomes. Am J Ophthalmol. 2018;192:38-47.

references.citation: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systemic Approach, 9th Edition. Elsevier. 2020.

sections.title: Red Flag Warning Signs
content: Rapidly growing hypopyon with thick fibrin plug in anterior chamber
Complete loss of red reflex with visual acuity dropped to Light Perception
Bleb melting or focal purulent blebitis in post-trabeculectomy eyes
Afferent pupillary defect (APD) or drop to No Light Perception (NLP)
Scleral thinning, corneal ring ulcer, or progression toward panophthalmitis

references.citation: Javitt JC, et al. National outcomes of cataract extraction: Endophthalmitis. Ophthalmology. 1991;98(6):899-906.

sections.title: Diagnostic & Microbiological Workup
content: Step 1: Emergency Assessment - Record BCVA, pupillary reactions, IOP, and slit-lamp findings.
Step 2: Diagnostic B-Scan Ultrasonography - Evaluate vitreous opacity, choroidal detachment, or retinal detachment.
Step 3: Intraocular Sampling - Perform 0.1 mL anterior chamber tap and 0.2-0.5 mL vitreous tap or needle biopsy.
Step 4: Microbiological Staining - Immediate Gram stain (lanceolate Gram-positive diplococci) and KOH preparation.
Step 5: Culture & Sensitivity - Inoculate directly onto blood agar, chocolate agar, and liquid thioglycollate media.
Step 6: Molecular Diagnostics - PCR assay for fastidious organisms or pre-treated cases.

references.citation: Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study Group. Results of the Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study. Arch Ophthalmol. 1995;113(12):1479-1496.

references.citation: Lemley CA, Han DP. Endophthalmitis: a review of current treatment strategies. Curr Opin Ophthalmol. 2007;18(3):236-243.

content.explanation: P: Prompt vitreous tap & intravitreal injections; N: Native coverage with Vancomycin + Ceftazidime; E: Early Vitrectomy consideration due to high virulence; U: Urgent topical fortified antibiotics; M: Monitor IOP and ultrasonography; O: Outcome depends on immediate intervention.

references.citation: AAO Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC), Section 09: Intraocular Inflammation and Uveitis. 2022-2023.

sections.title: Medical & Intravitreal Treatment Protocol
content: Step 1: Intravitreal Antibiotic Injection - Vancomycin 1.0 mg in 0.1 mL PLUS Ceftazidime 2.25 mg in 0.1 mL.
Step 2: Adjunctive Corticosteroid - Intravitreal Dexamethasone 0.4 mg in 0.1 mL (to dampen pneumolysin-induced tissue damage).
Step 3: Topical Fortified Drops - Fortified Vancomycin (50 mg/mL) and Tobramycin (14 mg/mL) alternating every 1 hour.
Step 4: Topical Steroids & Cycloplegics - Prednisolone acetate 1% q1h (after 24 hrs) and Atropine 1% BID.
Step 5: Systemic Antibiotics - Oral Moxifloxacin 400 mg daily or IV Vancomycin in cases with systemic/scleral extension.

references.citation: Schoenberger JE, et al. Modern management of bacterial endophthalmitis. Surv Ophthalmol. 2017;62(5):680-689.

sections.title: Surgical Indications & Vitrectomy (PPV)
content: EVS vs Clinical Reality: While the EVS recommended vitrectomy mainly for Light Perception (LP) vision, pneumococcal endophthalmitis often mandates early Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) even with better vision due to extreme bacterial virulence.
Surgical Goals: Immediate reduction of intraocular bacterial load, removal of toxic pneumolysin, clearing of dense vitreous debris, and improved antibiotic penetration.
Technique Pearls: Use complete 23-gauge or 25-gauge micro-incision vitrectomy system (MIVS); avoid aggressive posterior hyaloid peeling over necrotic retina to prevent iatrogenic retinal tears.
Post-Surgical Injections: Re-inject intravitreal Vancomycin (1.0 mg) and Ceftazidime (2.25 mg) at the conclusion of PPV.

references.citation: Kuhn F, Gini G. Vitrectomy for endophthalmitis. Ophthalmology. 2005;112(3):438-441.
Miller JJ, et al. Endophthalmitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Ophthalmology. 2004;111(8):1555-1559.

sections.title: Complications & Long-Term Sequelae
content: Tractional & Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment (occurs in up to 30% of cases).
Phthisis Bulbi and Complete Hypotony/Ocular Atrophy.
Ischemic Maculopathy & Retinal Artery/Vein Occlusions.
Secondary Neovascular Glaucoma secondary to chronic ocular ischemia.
Panophthalmitis with extraocular extension and orbital cellulitis.

references.citation: Espinosa-Barveri F, et al. Complications and visual outcomes in streptococcal endophthalmitis. Eur J Ophthalmol. 2021;31(4):1892-1899.

sections.title: High-Yield Clinical Pearls
content: Pneumococcal endophthalmitis carries a significantly worse visual prognosis than Staphylococcus epidermidis or culture-negative cases.
Filtering bleb-associated infection by S. pneumoniae can occur months to years after trabeculectomy; patient education on 'bleb red flags' is essential.
Direct Gram stain showing lanceolate Gram-positive diplococci provides an immediate rationale for aggressive combined intravitreal and surgical management.
Adjunctive intravitreal corticosteroids (Dexamethasone) help reduce host-mediated inflammatory retinal damage triggered by bacterial autolysis.

references.citation: Relhan N, et al. Endophthalmitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae: clinical features and outcomes. Am J Ophthalmol. 2018;192:38-47.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Evidence
sections.content: Recent epidemiological studies highlight increasing fluoroquinolone and penicillin resistance among ocular S. pneumoniae isolates, re-affirming Vancomycin as the indispensable intravitreal empiric standard. Furthermore, contemporary retrospective series demonstrate that early pars plana vitrectomy performed within 24–48 hours of presentation yields superior visual preservation and lower rates of phthisis bulbi compared to delayed surgical intervention in streptococcal endophthalmitis.

references.citation: Asbell PA, et al. Antibiotic susceptibility trends in ocular pathogens: ARMOR study updates. JAMA Ophthalmol. 2020;138(5):525-533.
